entities.summary:
Ibi, a renowned ancient Egyptian noble, played a pivotal role as chief steward of the God's Wife of Amun, Nitocris I, during the reign of pharaoh Psamtik I of the 26th Dynasty.

As the chief administrator of the temple, Ibi oversaw the management of the vast estates and resources under the god Amun, ensuring the prosperity of the temple and the pharaoh's power.

Ibi's expertise and influence extended beyond the temple, as he was involved in diplomatic missions and negotiations with neighboring kingdoms, further solidifying Egypt's position as a dominant force in the ancient world.

Despite the passing of centuries, Ibi's legacy remains a testament to the enduring power of ancient Egyptian administration and the importance of a well-organized state.

As the Roman historian Herodian once said, 'The gods are not pleased with those who neglect their duties.' Ibi's dedication to his duties and his unwavering commitment to the service of the gods have left an indelible mark on the annals of history.
